newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST - HUNGARY BILL, BOND YIELDS SEEN FALLING.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - HUNGARY BILL, BOND YIELDS SEEN FALLING.

text.p: Yields on Hungarian government securities are likely to drop on the secondary market this week amid abundant commercial bank liquidity and expectations of repo rate cuts for next Monday, dealers said.

"I expect a fall (in yields) on the OTC (over-the-counter) market," said Gyula Kerdo of Creditanstalt Securities. "There is enormous liquidity on the market due to maturing government papers and interest payments on them."
A dealer said the government's payments on its securities could bring some 80 billion forint extra liquidity for banks.

Dealers said most discount Treasury bill yields were likely to remain close to current levels, but one-year T-bill yields would probably drop to about 20.00 percent from the current levels of some 20.30 percent.
"The one-year (T-bill) is likely to fall substantially, its yield makes it seem a good investment, it is well above the yields on two- and three-year papers," said Zsolt Bango of Gog securities.
Government bond yields are seen easing 0.2 to 0.3 percent this week, continuing last week's trend.

The yields on these papers, which have maturities from two to seven years, dropped 0.3 to 0.4 percent last week after the announcement of the reduction of the monthly forint devaluation rate to 1.1 percent on April 1 from the current 1.2 percent.

The 2.2 percent rise in the CPI in February, published last week, was seen as positive and could also help the decline in yields, although its impact may have been built in prices already, dealers added.
Many market players expected the National Bank of Hungary to reduce its repo rates on Monday, they said, but the cut did not happen.
Thus expectations of repo cuts for next Monday were likely to strengthen, and this could also motor the decline in yields, dealers added.
